This page is a general guide on opening the box, sorting the bricks and starting to build. It has no model building step, so it adds no pieces or joins.

Step 1: white 4x12 plate (b1) is the base canvas. Step 2: two red 2x4 tiles (b3, b4) and two red 2x2 wedge plates (b2, b5, one at each end, the second rotated 180 degrees) cover two rows along one long edge of b1, which makes a red strip 12 studs long. The strip is read as the back two rows.

The `parts` and `edges` fields are the only way to record pieces in this schema. I filled them with this page's pieces, with rests_on as joined edges to b1 and colour in props. The other_joins list is empty.
Step 3: two red 1x2 tiles (b6, b7) go in the front row beside the end wedges, and one red 2x4 tile (b8) goes in the middle of the front two rows. All of them sit on the base plate b1.

Step 4: two blue 2x8 plates (b9, b10) are placed either side of the red 2x4 tile. They run front to back, with about 2 studs on b1 and the rest overhanging the front edge. I could not tell from the drawing whether they also touch the red pieces, so I listed only b1 in rests_on.
The schema has no pieces/rests_on fields, so the pieces are recorded as `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge. The other_joins list is empty.

Step 5: two white 4x12 plates (b11, b12) are added in front of the base plate b1, one behind the other, so the canvas is now roughly 12 studs square. They sit under the overhanging blue 2x8 plates (b9, b10), and their studs clutch the underside of those plates. Because they are underneath, their rests_on is empty. The joins are recorded as joined edges from b9 and b10 down to b11 and b12.
b11 touches b1 and b12 along their edges. The only fastening between those plates is through the blue plates, so these two edges are contact, not joined.
Which blue plate covers which studs is judged from the drawing. I took each blue plate to span both new plates.
The schema has no pieces or other_joins fields, so the new pieces are in `parts` and every join is an edge.
Step 6: four red 2x4 tiles form a red border down each side of the canvas, two per side (b13 and b14 on the left, b15 and b16 on the right). They run front to back next to the blue plates.
I assumed the rear tile on each side (b13, b15) covers b1 and b11, and the front tile (b14, b16) covers b11 and b12. The exact row offsets are judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge. The other_joins list is empty.

Step 7: a yellow 2x10 plate (b17) goes between the blue plates, starting just in front of the red 2x4 tile (b8). A light bluish gray 1x8 tile (b18, b19) goes on each side of it. The yellow plate overhangs the front edge of the canvas by about 2 studs.
I took the three new pieces to rest on b11 and b12 only, because b8 sits behind them and does not go under them. The exact row offsets are judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge. The other_joins list is empty.
Step 8: one white 4x12 plate (b20) is added in front of b12, which makes the canvas 12 x 16 studs. The overhanging front end of the yellow 2x10 plate (b17) sits on its studs, so b17 is joined to b20.
b20 touches b12 along their edges. They are not fastened to each other directly, so that edge is contact.
b20 is underneath b17, so its rests_on is empty. The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the piece is in `parts` and the join is an edge.

Step 9: two red 1x2 tiles (b21, b22) and four red 2x4 tiles (b23 to b26) are added. They fill in the front part of the red area on the left and right of the canvas and around the front tip of the yellow plate. The red now frames the front of the canvas.

The drawing is hard to read here, so the exact positions are my best guess. I took b23 and b25 to straddle b12 and b20, and b24, b26, b21 and b22 to sit on b20 only. I did not list the yellow plate b17 or the gray tiles as supports for these pieces.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge. The other_joins list is empty.

Step 10: four red 1x2 tiles (b28 to b31) fill the remaining front-edge gaps. A red 2x6 plate (b27) with its studs showing is laid along the front, just in front of the yellow plate. These studs are left open for later steps.
The drawing is hard to read, so I put all five new pieces on b20 only. They may also touch the tiles from step 9, but I could not confirm that.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge. The other_joins list is empty.
Step 11: two black 2x4 plates go on the back corners of the red frame, one at the upper left (b32) and one at the upper right (b33). They are the base for Mickey's ears.

Only the end wedge plates (b2 on the left, b5 on the right) have open studs there, because the 2x4 tiles have none. I recorded the plates as joined to the wedges. They also rest on the tiles beside them, b3 on the left and b4 on the right, which I recorded as contact. The exact overlap is judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and the joins are edges.

Step 12: a blue 2x4 tile (b34) goes on the middle of the yellow 2x10 plate (b17). A black 2x2 plate with 2 studs (b35, b36) goes on each side of it, one at each end. The front 2x2 of the yellow plate is left uncovered.
The two black plates are placed with their studs facing away from the blue tile. All three pieces rest only on b17.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 13: two black 4x8 half-round plates (b37, b38) are placed with their straight edges facing each other. Together they make a round black disc (Mickey's face or head) with a gap down the middle where the blue tile b34 shows.

The left half (b37) sits on the left blue plate b9, the left gray tile b18 and the black 2x2 plates b35 and b36. The right half (b38) sits on the right blue plate b10, the right gray tile b19, and b35 and b36. Which studs each half takes on b35 and b36 is judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 14: four black pieces are added at the front left of the canvas, over the red 2x6 plate with open studs (b27). They are a 2x4 plate (b39), a 2x4 wedge plate (b40), a left 2x2 wedge plate (b41) and a right 2x2 wedge plate (b42). Together they form one black shape, probably a shoe.

I put all four on b27 only, because it is the only piece in that spot with open studs. The tiles beside it have no studs. The wedge plates at the far front end may overhang b27, so the exact stud use is judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.
Step 15: one black 2x4 wedge plate (b43) is placed across the back of the gap in the black disc, between the two ear plates. It bridges both half-round plates, b37 and b38.
The part in the box looks like the second black 2x4 wedge plate (lego-51739). That is the only black wedge of that size in the parts list.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the piece is in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 16: a white 2x6 double round-corner plate (b44, lego-18980, curved on both long sides) goes on the black disc above the blue tile. It is the white face area. Two black 1x2 tiles (b45, b46) go on the disc beside it.
The drawing shows one tile being lowered onto the left half, with two green arrows. The box says 2x, so I assumed the second tile goes on the right half as a mirror. This is a guess.
I took the white plate to rest on both disc halves, b37 and b38. The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.
Step 17: a black 2x2 left wedge plate (b47) and a black 2x2 right wedge plate (b48) go on the black disc, one at each side of the white plate b44, to shape the face.
I assumed b47 rests on the left disc half (b37) and b48 on the right half (b38). They may also touch the black tiles b45 and b46 beside them, but I could not confirm that.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 18: two black 6x6 round plates (b49, b50) are the ears. The left ear (b49) sits on the upper-left black plate b32 and overlaps the left disc half b37. The right ear (b50) sits on b33 and overlaps the right disc half b38.
How much each ear overlaps the disc is judged from the drawing. The ears do not seem to cover the wedge plates b43, b47 or b48.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 19: two white 4x4 round-corner plates (b52 on the left, b53 on the right) and a white 2x3 plate (b51) cover the lower part of the black disc to make the white face. The 2x3 plate goes below the blue tile, between the two corner plates. The white 2x6 plate b44 is above the blue tile.
I assumed b52 sits on the left disc half b37, b53 on the right half b38, and b51 bridges both. The exact stud overlap is judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 20: six pieces are added over the black shoe shape at the front left of the canvas, built in step 14. They are a white 2x2 tile (b54), a white 1x2 jumper plate with one stud (b55), two black 1x2 tiles (b56, b57), and black 2x2 wedge plates, one left (b58) and one right (b59). They add the white spat and the black toe details.

The drawing is small, so which black piece each new piece sits on is a guess. b54 and b56 go on b39. b55 and b57 go on b40. b58 goes on b41 and b59 goes on b42. Some of them may bridge two of those pieces.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 21: the model is turned over so the underside of the four white base plates (b1, b11, b12, b20) faces up. Two white 1x16 bricks (b60, b61) go along the two long sides, and a white 1x10 brick (b62) goes across one end between them. This makes a raised frame.
I took the 1x10 brick to sit at the front end, over b20. The black shoe pieces are visible under that end in the drawing. The far end of the frame is open. Each 1x16 brick spans all four base plates.

b62 touches the ends of b60 and b61 along their sides, so those edges are contact. The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 22: a white 1x10 plate (b63) closes the open far end of the frame, between the two 1x16 bricks b60 and b61. It sits on the underside of the back base plate b1, and its ends touch the two long bricks.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the piece is in `parts` and the rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 23: a light bluish gray 1x4 plate (b66) goes in the middle of the white 1x10 plate b63. A white 1x3 plate (b64, b65) goes on each side of it. That fills all 10 studs of b63. The drawing shows one white plate being lowered by the red arrows. I took the other to be the one already placed at the right end.
All three plates rest on b63. The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 24: a white 3x2 plate with a rounded end and a hole (b67) and two white 1x2 hinge plates (b68, b69) are added on the plates at the end of the frame (b64, b65, b66). The red arrows show one hinge plate (b68) being lowered. The other (b69) is already in place on the other side of the rounded plate. They begin the stand that holds the frame up.

The drawing is small, so which plate each piece sits on is a guess. b67 is on b66 and b64, b68 is on b66, and b69 is on b65. I did not record the hinge fingers pairing with anything yet, because no mating part appears on this page.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 25: the second white 1x10 plate (b70) goes across the end of the frame between the two 1x16 bricks, on the row next to b63. It sits on the studs of the base plate b1. The hinge pieces from step 24 stay uncovered.
The drawing does not show clearly which studs it clutches, so I recorded it only against b1. Its ends touch b60 and b61, so those edges are contact.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the piece is in `parts` and the rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.
Page 32 (step 26) is a separate sub-assembly, the U-shaped handle or arm piece. It is not yet attached to the model.

Sub-step 1: the red 2-long notched axle (b73) is pushed into the end hole of the first white elbow tube (b71). Sub-step 2: a second elbow (b72) is put on the other end of the red axle, so the two elbows form a U. Sub-step 3: a gray 11-long axle (b74, b75) is pushed into each free end hole.
The parts box also shows two white hinge cylinders (lego-57360, 2x). They are not used on this page, so they are not added yet. The two parts are labelled (11) for axle length.
The elbow ports used are axle-hole.1 and axle-hole.2. Which hole of each elbow takes which axle is my assumption.

Step 4 (page 33): a white hinge cylinder (b76, b77) goes on the free end of each gray axle, b74 and b75. The finished U-shaped stand is then clicked onto the two hinge plates b68 and b69 at the end of the frame. It folds on those hinges, so it is a revolute joint.

The hinge cylinders are the two lego-57360 parts listed in the parts box on page 32 but not used there. The cylinder's axle hole is used for the axle. Which of the cylinder's two hinge ports (hinge.1 or hinge.2) mates with each plate is my assumption.
No new pieces besides the cylinders. The schema has no pieces or other_joins fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and all joins are edges.

Step 27: four light bluish gray round 1x1 bricks (b78 to b81) are pressed onto the four corner studs of the frame, two on each long brick. The red arrow shows one being placed near the front on the left brick. They look like feet for the back of the frame.
Assignment: b78 and b79 go on the left 1x16 brick b60, at its near and far ends. b80 and b81 go on the right brick b61, at its far and near ends. The corner positions are judged from the drawing.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 28: a white round 2x2 plate with a rounded bottom (boat stud) goes on each of the four gray round bricks at the corners of the frame (b82 on b79, b83 on b80, b84 on b78, b85 on b81). They act as rounded feet. The 'rounded bottom' faces up and sits on the brick stud.
A 2x2 round plate is bigger than a 1x1 round brick, so it may also overhang the long brick. I recorded only the round brick as the support, because the single boat stud clutches only that stud.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 29: the model is turned back face up. The third black 4x8 half-round plate (b86) goes across the top of the face and makes Mickey's black hair or head-top. It covers the black wedge plates b43, b47 and b48 and the upper edges of the disc halves b37 and b38.
How far the plate reaches down over the white crescent b44 is hard to tell, so I did not list b44 as a support. The black tiles b45 and b46 have no open studs, so they are not listed either.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the piece is in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 30: a light bluish gray 3x4 plate with a 1x4 centre row of studs (b87) goes on the black hair plate b86. A white round 3x3 tile (b88, b89) goes at each side of the face, one on the upper left and one on the lower right.
The drawing is hard to read here, so which pieces each one sits on is judged. I took b87 on b86 only. I took b88 on b86, b44 and b37. I took b89 on b86, b53 and b38.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 31: a white 2x6 double round-corner plate (b90) is the third and last of its type. It goes on the white lower face (muzzle), and a yellow 1x2 rounded plate (b91) with two open studs goes on top of it. The two yellow cut-corner wedge plates (b92, b93) go on the black shoe at the front left. They are a yellow bow or shoe detail.
The drawing is small, so the exact supports are guesses. b90 is on b44 and b51, b91 is on b90, b92 is on b40, and b93 is on b55 and b42. The yellow wedges may also bridge other black pieces.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.

Step 32: a yellow round 2x2 tile (b94) goes on the two yellow wedge plates (b92, b93) and makes the knot of the bow. A white 2x3 plate (b97, the second lego-3021) goes on the head top over the gray plate b87 and the black plate b86. Two white round quarter tiles (b95, b96) are also added.

The box icon for the white plate shows a plate with more than 6 studs. The parts list only has a second white lego-3021 (2x3) left, so I used that. The white quarter tiles are tiny in the drawing and I could not see where they go. I put them on b97, which may be wrong, and they may belong on the white face instead.
The schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the pieces are in `parts` and each rests_on is recorded as a joined edge.
